objective: Keep action-menu focus,selection and outside dismissal consistent with the scoped ARIA menu-button keyboard contract.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Accessible action menus remain practical application controls.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Tab must leave without a keyboard trap or focus being stolen back.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Native default actions,blur relatedTarget,ref containment,unique ids and effect-owned listeners transfer.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The existing thirty-five-minute level14tier4exercise already supplies menu structure and keyboard scaffolding.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Wrong containment or prevented Tab can close inside interactions or trap keyboard users.

defects: Original already checked wrapping,Home/End,ArrowDown opening,Enter/click choices,Escape,inside/outside mousedown and listener lifetime.
All original boards kept the menu open when focus left via Tab;the brief claimed APG behavior without this required close.

Add menu onBlur closing only when relatedTarget leaves,without preventDefault or focus return;give junior an Actions menu name,useId for reference optional controls,and update senior latest callback in an effect. An additional control that removes only the focus-leave handler still fails the Tab assertion in both the server worker and actual browser,so the requirement is retained.
